points.text: No convergence or approximation analysis of surrogate fidelity to full LLM
No quantitative metrics of proxy fidelity to LLM across domains
Memory and runtime scalability of extra models not analyzed
Validation set choice (LAMBADA) may bias selection; no robustness analysis
No analysis of what kinds of data the learned scores prefer
Ablation gains marginal; statistical significance not substantiated
Missing comparison with ALinFiK influence estimation method
Differences and advantages versus ALinFiK not discussed
Motivation for proxy model instead of original LLM not justified
Experiments only on C4; generalizability to other corpora unclear
No ablation on number of rounds or other key hyperparameters
Functions F and G mentioned but not introduced
From-scratch claim contradicted by random warm-up and KL with partially trained LLM
Proxy not trained to convergence (3000 steps, reset); long-term impact claim unsupported
No convergence guarantees, approximation bounds or theory for bilevel formulation
FLOPs comparison with MATES unreasonable given differing operations and parallelization
Memory overhead of two additional models not accounted
Wall-clock time comparisons absent
Many main improvements within standard error margins
No analysis with differing proxy and target architectures
Recent data selection methods (DCLM, QuRating, Meta-rater, QUAD) not compared
Cost of external-model methods not fairly accounted versus bilevel optimization
Average improvements over MATES within reported errors
Experiment scale insufficient for pretraining; generalization to larger models questionable
Manually specified validation set in pretraining may hurt generalization
Practical relevance of small-scale from-scratch pretraining setting questionable
Need for quality subset selection versus coarse filtering not motivated
Gains small relative to noise; no seed variance or significance tests
1.7x speedup claim loosely defined, single run, one baseline
Reported number inconsistencies (FLOPs entry, 2.8B vs 2.5B)
Differing Round 1 random rows imply run variance as large as gains
Ablation (Table 5) gaps within noise and inconsistent with Table 1
Baseline framing questionable: MATES also trains from scratch without external LLMs
No evidence that long-term influence is source of gain
Proxy trained only 3000 steps; not trained to convergence
Named baselines (DsDm, LESS, QuRating, DSIR, SemDeDup) not reported
Validation tasks overlap evaluation tasks; leakage not discussed
Downstream-aligned validation data acts as oracle; from-scratch qualified
Softmax partial-sum approximation changes objective; only in appendix
Run algorithm differs from analyzed; no convergence or hypergradient checks
Non-convex lower level; implicit gradient formula does not apply
No analysis of what data is selected
Compute advantage holds only at 1B; inference FLOPs exceed MATES
No wall-clock or GPU-hours reported
Missing cheap same-proxy baseline such as perplexity-based selection
Scale limited: 2.8B with 15B tokens on data selected for 1B
Only C4 and top-20% selection used
Zero-shot evaluation near chance; no held-out perplexity
State-of-the-art claim overstated
